title: Java For Loop
learningObjectives: Identify initialization, condition and update parts of a for loop.
Use a for loop to repeat a task a known number of times.
Control loop direction and step size with an update expression.
Use nested loops for simple row-and-column patterns.
Choose between indexed and enhanced for loops based on whether the task needs positions or only element values.

understand.concept: A for loop places initialization, a boolean condition and an update expression in one header. The initialization runs once; the condition is checked before each iteration; the update runs after each completed iteration.
understand.whyItMatters: For loops are concise when processing a known range, counting, traversing indexes or generating repeated patterns.
understand.analogy: A decision or repetition rule is like a clear instruction: test the stated condition, then follow the matching path.
understand.analogyLimit: A program condition is evaluated exactly according to Java's boolean and operator rules; real-world decisions may require additional validation.

explain.narrative:
## The for loop header

The general form is `for (initialization; condition; update)`. Initialization runs once, the condition is checked before each iteration, and update runs after the body.

## Counting and stepping

Use `i++` to increase a counter by one, `i--` to decrease it, or another expression such as `i += 2` to use a different step.

## Nested loops

A loop inside another loop is a nested loop. The inner loop completes its iterations for each iteration of the outer loop.

## Common mistakes

- Using a condition that excludes or adds an unintended boundary value.
- Updating in the wrong direction.
- Accidentally using a step that never reaches the stopping condition.
- Confusing the loop variable's scope with a variable declared outside the loop.
- Creating too many iterations in nested loops.

## The enhanced for loop (for-each)

The enhanced for loop visits each element of an array or an object that implements `Iterable` without requiring an index variable. Use it when you need each value in sequence. Use a traditional indexed for loop when you need the element position, want to update an array slot by index, or need to traverse only part of an array. Reassigning the loop variable does not replace the corresponding array element.

examples.title: Count from one to five
examples.explanation: The loop starts at 1, continues while i is at most 5, and increments after each iteration.

examples.title: Count backwards
examples.explanation: The counter decreases and the loop ends after it becomes zero.

examples.title: Use a step of two
examples.explanation: The update expression adds two each time, so only even values in this range are printed.

examples.title: Calculate a total with a for loop
examples.explanation: The loop adds each integer from 1 through 5 to the running total.

examples.title: Nested loops and enhanced for traversal
examples.explanation: The inner loop completes three products for each outer row. The enhanced for loop then visits every mark without exposing its index and adds each value to total.

practise.guidedTask: Use a traditional for loop to print the indexes and values of an integer array. Use an enhanced for loop to calculate the total of the same array. Then change one element by index and explain why reassigning the enhanced-for loop variable would not update the array slot.
practise.independentTask: Create a weekly sales report from an array. Use an indexed loop to update the value at a selected position, and an enhanced for loop to calculate the total and average. Include an empty-array case and explain how you avoid division by zero.
hints: The for header initializes once, tests before each iteration and updates after the body; verify the boundary and step direction.
Use enhanced for when you need each array or Iterable element but not its index; assigning the loop variable does not replace an array slot.
In nested loops, the inner loop completes for each outer iteration; estimate the total iteration count before choosing large bounds.
practise.challenge: Compare nested loops with an enhanced for loop. Choose the loop form that best fits each task: accessing an element's index, reading every value, and printing a two-dimensional pattern.

questions.prompt: Which part of a for loop runs once before the first condition check?
questions.explanation: Initialization establishes the starting state once.

questions.prompt: When does the update expression run?
options: After the loop body completes an iteration
Only when the condition is false
questions.answer: After the loop body completes an iteration
questions.explanation: The update runs after each completed body iteration.

questions.prompt: Which update expression increases i by two?
questions.explanation: Compound addition increases the variable by the specified amount.

options: A loop placed inside another loop
A loop used only for Strings
questions.answer: A loop placed inside another loop
questions.explanation: The inner loop runs as part of the outer loop's body.

questions.prompt: When is an enhanced for loop most suitable?
options: When visiting each element without needing its index
When changing elements by a specific index
When skipping directly to an arbitrary index
questions.answer: When visiting each element without needing its index
questions.explanation: The enhanced for loop is concise for sequential element traversal when an index is unnecessary.
